title: Glacial Processes & Erosional Landforms
welcome_lead: Link processes to upland glacial landforms.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on glacial erosion processes and the landforms they create.
final_note: Plucking and abrasion sculpt corries and U-valleys.

concepts.def: Meltwater freezes around bedrock, pulls fragments away as ice moves.
Embedded debris scrapes bedrock like sandpaper, creating striations.
Water freezes in cracks, expands 9 percent, fractures rock; supplies debris.
Armchair-shaped hollow on mountainside; e.g. Red Tarn, Lake District.
Straight, steep-sided trough; e.g. Lauterbrunnen, Switzerland.
Knife-edge ridge between two corries; e.g. Striding Edge, Helvellyn.

walkthroughs.body_html: Plucking dominates where bedrock is well-jointed; abrasion produces fine rock flour and polished surfaces with striations indicating ice direction. Rate depends on ice thickness, velocity and debris load; Alpine glaciers erode at 0.1-1 mm/yr typically.

Snow accumulates in north-facing hollows, compacts to firn then ice. Rotational flow erodes downward and backward. Red Tarn beneath Helvellyn is a classic UK example. Three adjacent corries meeting form a pyramidal peak like Snowdon or Matterhorn.

Glaciers straighten and overdeepen pre-existing V-valleys, creating troughs. Lauterbrunnen Valley (Switzerland) is 600 m deep with vertical walls. Hanging valleys (e.g. Staubbach Falls 297 m) form where tributary glaciers meet the main trunk.

What causes global sea level rise?
options: A tipping point is when world leaders agree to act on climate change.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.

mcqs.q: What is a positive climate feedback loop?
options: Positive feedback means the climate balances itself out.
A tipping point is when world leaders agree to act on climate change.
A process where warming triggers changes that cause more warming — e.g. melting Arctic ice exposes dark ocean, which absorbs more heat, melting more ice (ice-albedo feedback).
Positive feedback means a good outcome for the climate.

mcqs.q: What is a climate tipping point?
options: A tipping point is when world leaders agree to act on climate change.
A threshold beyond which a system changes irreversibly into a new state — e.g. the Amazon flipping from rainforest to savanna, or Greenland's ice sheet committing to total melt.
A tipping point is just when warming reaches 1.5 degrees C.
Positive feedback means the climate balances itself out.
